subject: maths
title: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages
seo_title: Year 6 Fractions, Decimals and Percentages Worksheets: 3/8 = 0.375, Equivalents and Ordering
standard_text: Associate a fraction with division and calculate decimal fraction equivalents [for example, 0.375] for a simple fraction [for example, 3/8]; identify the value of each digit in numbers given to three decimal places; recall and use equivalences between simple fractions, decimals and percentages, including in different contexts.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 fractions, decimals and percentages worksheets for the National Curriculum: place value to three decimal places, fractions as division (3/8 = 0.375), equivalents such as 1/5 = 0.2 = 20%, ordering mixed forms and SATs-style problems. 100 maths questions with an answer key.
key_big: A fraction is a division: 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. Per cent means out of 100: 0.375 = 37.5%.
key_sub: Know the key facts: 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%, 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%, 1/5 = 0.2 = 20%, 1/8 = 0.125 = 12.5%. To compare, change everything into decimals with the same number of places.
body_html:
Place value to three decimal places

After the decimal point come tenths, then hundredths, then thousandths. 1 tenth = 10 hundredths = 100 thousandths. A 0 holds an empty place.

A fraction is a division

38 means 3 ÷ 8. To change a fraction into a decimal, divide the numerator by the denominator. Write the number being divided with a decimal point and some zeros, then use short division.

Quicker way

Write 720 as a decimal.

Make the denominator 100: 20 × 5 = 100, so multiply the top by 5 too. 720 = 35100.

Answer: 0.35

Fractions, decimals and percentages

Per cent means out of 100. To change a decimal into a percentage, multiply by 100: 0.4 = 40%. To change a percentage into a decimal, divide by 100: 7% = 0.07.

Comparing and ordering

Change everything into the same form first. Decimals with the same number of places are easiest to compare.

Example

Order 0.35, 38 and 37% from smallest to greatest.

0.35 = 0.350. 38 = 0.375. 37% = 0.370. Compare 350, 370 and 375 thousandths.

Answer: 0.35, 37%, 38

Who did better?

Freya scored 21 out of 25. George scored 17 out of 20.

2125 = 84100 = 84%. 1720 = 85100 = 85%.

Answer: George, with the higher percentage

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
38 = 0.38 or 3.8Divide: 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375
15 = 0.5 or 15%15 = 210 = 0.2 = 20%
0.4 = 4%0.4 = 0.40 = 40%
0.305 > 0.35 because it has more digitsUse 3 places: 0.305 < 0.350
The 7 in 4.007 is 7 hundredthsThe third place is thousandths: 0.007
7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3 = 1.3Divide the remainder too: 34 = 0.75, so 1.75

faq.q: What fractions, decimals and percentages do children learn in Year 6?
faq.a: In Year 6 children find decimal equivalents of fractions by dividing (3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375), read the value of each digit up to three decimal places, and use equivalences such as 1/5 = 0.2 = 20% and 3/4 = 0.75 = 75% to compare and solve problems.

faq.q: How do you change a fraction into a decimal?
faq.a: Divide the numerator by the denominator, for example 3/8 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375 using short division. If the denominator goes into 10, 100 or 1,000, you can make an equivalent fraction instead: 7/20 = 35/100 = 0.35.

faq.q: How do you order fractions, decimals and percentages?
faq.a: Change them all into decimals with the same number of decimal places, then compare. For 0.35, 3/8 and 37%: 0.350, 0.375 and 0.370, so the order is 0.35, 37%, 3/8.

faq.q: Are fractions, decimals and percentages in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. The KS2 SATs arithmetic paper and both reasoning papers often include them, such as writing a fraction as a decimal, ordering mixed numbers in different forms and comparing test scores as percentages.

sets.title: Place value to three decimal places

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 4.073?
items.e: The red 7 is in the hundredths column, the second place after the decimal point. Its value is 7 hundredths = 0.07.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 2.508?
items.e: The red 8 is in the thousandths column, the third place after the decimal point. Its value is 8 thousandths = 0.008. Thousandths are the third place, not the second.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 13.264?
items.e: The red 2 is in the tenths column, the first place after the decimal point. Its value is 2 tenths = 0.2.

items.q: What is the value of the red digit in 0.719?
items.e: The red 9 is in the thousandths column, the third place after the decimal point. Its value is 9 thousandths = 0.009. Thousandths are the third place, not the second.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 6 in 3.456?
items.e: In 3.456 the 6 is in the thousandths place (3rd after the decimal point). So its value is 6 thousandths = 0.006.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 3 in 5.638?
items.e: In 5.638 the 3 is in the hundredths place (2nd after the decimal point). So its value is 3 hundredths = 0.03.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 4 in 9.104?
items.e: In 9.104 the 4 is in the thousandths place (3rd after the decimal point). So its value is 4 thousandths = 0.004.

items.q: What is the value of the digit 8 in 12.875?
items.e: In 12.875 the 8 is in the tenths place (1st after the decimal point). So its value is 8 tenths = 0.8.

items.q: Write 3 ones, 4 tenths and 6 thousandths as a decimal.
items.e: There are 0 hundredths, so write a 0 to hold the hundredths place: 3 . 4 0 6 = 3.406. 3.46 would be 6 hundredths.
4 ones, 3 tenths, 0 hundredths and 8 thousandths: 4.308. The 0 holds the hundredths place.

items.q: Write 71000 as a decimal.
items.e: 71000 is 7 thousandths. Thousandths are the third place after the point, so write 0s in the tenths and hundredths places: 0.007.

items.q: Write 451000 as a decimal.
items.e: 45 thousandths = 4 hundredths and 5 thousandths. The last digit must be in the third place: 0.045. 0.45 would be 45 hundredths.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.239?
items.e: 0.239 has three decimal places, so the last digit is in the thousandths place: 239 thousandths = 2391000.
The 5 is in the hundredths place, so it is worth 5 hundredths = 0.05. Check: 6 + 0.2 + 0.05 + 0.004 = 6.254.

items.q: In which number is the digit 5 worth 5 thousandths?
items.e: Thousandths are the third place after the decimal point. Only 2.305 has the 5 there. In 2.053 the 5 is worth 5 hundredths.

items.q: How many thousandths are there in 0.1?
items.e: 1 tenth = 10 hundredths = 100 thousandths. 0.1 = 0.100.

items.q: What number is 1 thousandth more than 2.399?
items.e: 9 thousandths + 1 thousandth = 10 thousandths = 1 hundredth. That makes 10 hundredths = 1 tenth. So 2.399 + 0.001 = 2.400 = 2.4. 2.409 adds 1 hundredth, not 1 thousandth.

items.q: Which number is equal to 2.07?
items.e: A 0 at the end of a decimal does not change its value: 2.07 = 2.070. A 0 in the middle does: 2.7 and 2.007 are different numbers.

items.q: Which digit is in the thousandths place in 5.162?
items.e: Tenths, hundredths, thousandths: 5 . 1 6 2. The third digit after the point is 2. 6 is in the hundredths place.
Dividing by 1,000 moves every digit 3 places to the right. The 7 lands in the thousandths place: 0.047. 0.47 is 47 ÷ 100.

items.q: Which calculation is the same as 38?
items.e: A fraction is a division: the numerator is divided by the denominator. 38 = 3 ÷ 8.

items.q: 3 pizzas are shared equally between 4 children. How much pizza does each child get?
c: 13 of a pizza
43 of a pizza
34 of a pizza
14 of a pizza
items.e: 3 shared between 4 is 3 ÷ 4 = 34. Each pizza gives every child 14, and there are 3 pizzas.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 4 ÷ 9?
items.e: Divide 4 into 9 equal parts: each part is 49. So 4 ÷ 9 = 49. 94 is 9 ÷ 4.

items.q: Write 15 as a decimal.
items.e: 15 = 210, so 15 = 0.2. (Or 1 ÷ 5: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 tenths.) 5 is 5 ÷ 1, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 35 as a decimal.
items.e: 35 = 610 (multiply the top and bottom by 2). So 35 = 0.6.

items.q: Write 18 as a decimal.
items.e: 1 ÷ 8: write 1 as 1.000. 10 ÷ 8 = 1 r 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 r 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 18 = 0.125. Do not just write the digits 1 and 8 after the point.

items.q: The short division shows 3 ÷ 8. What is 38 as a decimal?
items.e: 30 ÷ 8 = 3 r 6, 60 ÷ 8 = 7 r 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.38 and 3.8 just use the digits of the fraction.

items.q: The short division shows 5 ÷ 8. What is 58 as a decimal?
items.e: 50 ÷ 8 = 6 r 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 r 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 5 ÷ 8 = 0.625. 1.6 is 8 ÷ 5: the division is the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 78 as a decimal.
items.e: 7 ÷ 8: 70 ÷ 8 = 8 r 6, 60 ÷ 8 = 7 r 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5. So 78 = 0.875. Keep dividing until there is no remainder: 0.87 stops too soon.

items.q: Write 68 as a decimal.
items.e: Simplify first: 68 = 34. 34 = 75100 = 0.75.

items.q: Write 225 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 225 = 8100 = 8 hundredths = 0.08. 0.8 would be 8 tenths.

items.q: Write 720 as a decimal.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 720 = 35100 = 0.35. Multiply the numerator by 5 too, not just the denominator.

items.q: Which division has the answer 0.4?
items.e: 2 ÷ 5 = 25 = 410 = 0.4. 5 ÷ 2 = 2.5, 4 ÷ 100 = 0.04 and 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25.

items.q: Write 74 as a decimal.
items.e: 7 ÷ 4 = 1 r 3. The remainder 3 still has to be divided by 4: 34 = 0.75. So 74 = 1.75. 1.3 writes the remainder as a decimal digit.
13 ÷ 5 = 2 r 3, and 3 ÷ 5 = 35 = 0.6. So 13 ÷ 5 = 2 35 = 2.6. The remainder 3 is not 0.3.

items.q: Write 2 38 as a decimal.
items.e: The 2 ones stay the same. 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. So 2 38 = 2.375.

items.q: Which fraction is equal to 0.125?
items.e: 0.125 = 1251000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 18. 125100 would be 1.25.

items.q: Write 940 as a decimal.
items.e: 40 × 25 = 1,000, so 940 = 2251000 = 0.225. (Or 9 ÷ 40: 9 ÷ 4 = 2.25, then ÷ 10 = 0.225.)

items.q: Write 13 as a decimal, rounded to 3 decimal places.
items.e: 1 ÷ 3 = 0.3333… The 3s go on for ever. To 3 decimal places, 13 = 0.333. 3 is 3 ÷ 1, the wrong way round.

items.q: Write 23 as a decimal, rounded to 3 decimal places.
items.e: 2 ÷ 3 = 0.6666… The 4th decimal place is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up: 0.667. 0.666 cuts the digits off without rounding.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is shaded?
items.e: 20 of the 100 squares are shaded. Per cent means out of 100, so it is 20%. This is also 15 = 0.2.

items.q: Which shows the shaded part as a decimal and a percentage?
items.e: 35 of 100 squares: 35100 = 0.35 = 35%. 0.65 and 65% describe the white part.

items.q: Write 15 as a percentage.
items.e: 15 = 20100 = 20%. (1 ÷ 5 = 0.2.) 15% just writes the digits 1 and 5.

items.q: Write 14 as a percentage.
items.e: 14 = 25100 = 25%. 4% and 40% use the 4 from the denominator.

items.q: Write 34 as a percentage.
items.e: 34 = 75100 = 75%. 25% is only 14.

items.q: Write 110 as a percentage.
items.e: 110 = 10100 = 10%. 1% is 1100.

items.q: Write 0.4 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.4 = 4 tenths = 40 hundredths = 40%. To change a decimal to a percentage, multiply by 100: 0.4 × 100 = 40.

items.q: Write 0.07 as a percentage.
items.e: 0.07 = 7 hundredths = 7%. 70% would be 0.7.

items.q: Write 45% as a decimal.
items.e: 45% = 45 hundredths = 0.45. Divide by 100: the digits move 2 places to the right.

items.q: Write 8% as a decimal.
items.e: 8% = 8 hundredths. Hundredths are the second place after the point: 0.08. 0.8 is 80%.

items.q: Write 25 as a decimal.
items.e: 25 = 410 = 0.4. 0.25 just writes the digits, 2.5 is 5 ÷ 2, and 0.2 is only 15.

items.q: What percentage of the hundred square is not shaded?
items.e: 4 squares are shaded, so 100 − 4 = 96 squares are white. 96 out of 100 = 96%.

items.q: Which of these is not equal to 34?
items.e: 34 = 0.75 = 75% = 68. 0.34 just writes the digits 3 and 4, so it is not equal.

items.q: Write 320 as a percentage.
items.e: 20 × 5 = 100, so 320 = 15100 = 15%. 60% comes from 3 × 20.

items.q: Write 925 as a percentage.
items.e: 25 × 4 = 100, so 925 = 36100 = 36%. 34% adds 9 and 25.

items.q: Write 60% as a fraction in its simplest form.
items.e: 60% = 60100 = 610. Divide the top and bottom by 2: 35. 350 is 6%.

items.q: Write 5% as a fraction in its simplest form.
items.e: 5% = 5100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 120. 15 is 20%, not 5%.

items.q: Write 18 as a percentage.
items.e: 18 = 1 ÷ 8 = 0.125. Multiply by 100: 0.125 × 100 = 12.5%.

items.q: Write 0.375 as a percentage.
items.e: Multiply by 100: the digits move 2 places to the left. 0.375 × 100 = 37.5, so 0.375 = 37.5%.

items.q: Write 1.2 as a percentage.
items.e: 1.2 × 100 = 120, so 1.2 = 120%. A number bigger than 1 is more than 100%.

sets.title: Compare and order fractions, decimals and percentages

items.q: Compare 0.35 and 0.305.
items.e: Write both with 3 decimal places: 0.350 and 0.305. Compare the hundredths: 5 > 0. So 0.35 > 0.305. More digits does not mean a bigger number.

items.q: Compare 0.7 and 0.65.
items.e: 0.7 = 0.70. Compare the tenths: 7 tenths > 6 tenths. So 0.7 > 0.65, even though 65 > 7.

items.q: Compare 0.09 and 0.1.
items.e: 0.1 = 0.10. Compare the tenths: 0 < 1. So 0.09 < 0.1.

items.q: Compare 0.6 and 35.
items.e: 35 = 610 = 0.6. So 0.6 = 35.

items.q: Compare 38 and 0.35.
items.e: Change the fraction to a decimal: 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.375 > 0.350, so 38 > 0.35.

items.q: Compare 40% and 0.04.
Compare 15 and 15%.
items.e: 15 = 20%. 20% > 15%, so 15 > 15%.

items.q: Compare 18 and 0.2.
items.e: 18 = 0.125 and 0.2 = 0.200. 0.125 < 0.200, so 18 < 0.2. 8 is bigger than 2, but eighths are smaller parts.

items.q: Compare 23 and 0.66.
items.e: 23 = 2 ÷ 3 = 0.666…, which is a little more than 0.66 = 0.660. So 23 > 0.66.

items.q: Which is the greatest?
items.e: As decimals: 0.450, 25 = 0.400, 42% = 0.420, 0.405. The greatest is 0.45.

items.q: Which is the smallest?
items.e: As decimals: 0.205, 14 = 0.250, 0.300, 22% = 0.220. The smallest is 0.205, even though it has the most digits.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
0.35, 38, 37%
items.e: Make them all decimals with 3 places: 0.350, 38 = 0.375, 37% = 0.370. So the order is 0.35, 37%, 38.

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
0.5, 0.45, 0.405, 0.054
Which number is between 0.3 and 0.4?
items.e: 38 = 0.375, which is between 0.3 and 0.4. 14 = 0.25 and 45% = 0.45 are not; 0.43 is more than 0.4.

items.q: The line from 0 to 1 is split into 8 equal parts. What decimal is at the red dot?
items.e: 8 equal parts, so each part is 18. The dot is 3 parts along: 38 = 3 ÷ 8 = 0.375. 0.3 would be 3 tenths, but the line has 8 parts, not 10.

items.q: The line from 0% to 100% is split into 5 equal parts. What percentage is at the red dot?
items.e: 5 equal parts, so each part is 15 = 20%. The dot is 4 parts along: 4 × 20% = 80%. 40% counts each part as 10%.

items.q:
Order from greatest to smallest:
0.8, 34, 79%
items.e: As decimals: 0.8 = 0.80, 34 = 0.75, 79% = 0.79. Greatest first: 0.8, 79%, 34.

items.q: Which list is in order, smallest first?
items.e: 0.6 = 0.600, 23 = 0.666… and 70% = 0.700. So 0.6, 23, 70%.

items.q: Which number is greater than 14 but less than 13?
items.e: 14 = 0.25 and 13 = 0.333… 0.3 is between them. 35% = 0.35 is more than 0.333…

items.q:
Order from smallest to greatest:
1.2, 115%, 1 14
items.e: As decimals: 1.2 = 1.20, 115% = 1.15, 1 14 = 1.25. So 115%, 1.2, 1 14.

sets.title: Fractions, decimals and percentages in context

items.q: Mohammed scores 18 out of 20 in a spelling test. What percentage does he score?
items.e: 1820 = 90100 (multiply the top and bottom by 5) = 90%. 10% is the part he got wrong.

items.q: In a maths test, Ethan scores 21 out of 25 and Aisha scores 17 out of 20. Who has the higher percentage?
items.e: 2125 = 84100 = 84%. 1720 = 85100 = 85%. 85% > 84%, so Aisha does better, even with fewer marks.

items.q: A shop sign says 25% off. What fraction of the price is taken off?
items.e: 25% = 25100 = 14. 34 is what you still pay.

items.q: Shop A has 14 off a coat. Shop B has 20% off the same coat. Which shop takes off more?
items.e: 14 = 25%, and 25% > 20%. The coat is the same price to start with, so Shop A takes off more.

items.q: In a class, 35 of the pupils walk to school. What percentage of the class walk?
items.e: 35 = 60100 = 60%. 35% just writes the digits 3 and 5.

items.q: 0.7 of the pupils in Year 6 have school dinners. The rest have a packed lunch. What percentage have a packed lunch?
items.e: 0.7 = 70% have school dinners. The whole year group is 100%, so 100% − 70% = 30% have a packed lunch.

items.q: Freya cuts a 3 m ribbon into 4 equal pieces. How long is each piece?
items.e: 3 ÷ 4 = 34 m = 0.75 m. 1.33 m is 4 ÷ 3, the wrong way round. 0.25 m would be a 1 m ribbon.

items.q: 5 pizzas are shared equally between 8 children. How much pizza does each child get, as a decimal?
items.e: 5 ÷ 8 = 58. 50 ÷ 8 = 6 r 2, 20 ÷ 8 = 2 r 4, 40 ÷ 8 = 5, so each child gets 0.625 of a pizza. 1.6 is 8 ÷ 5.

items.q: Oliver’s tablet battery shows 45%. What fraction of a full charge is that?
items.e: 45% = 45100. Divide the top and bottom by 5: 920. 451000 is 0.045 = 4.5%.

items.q: A football team won 12 of its 16 matches. What percentage of its matches did it win?
items.e: 1216 = 34 (divide by 4) = 75%. 25% is the matches it did not win.

items.q: A carton of fruit juice is 38 apple juice and 40% orange juice. Is there more apple or orange juice?
items.e: 38 = 0.375 = 37.5%. 40% > 37.5%, so there is more orange juice.

items.q: Kai scores 33 out of 40 in a reading test. Harry scores 82%. Who has the higher score?
items.e: 3340 = 33 ÷ 40 = 0.825 = 82.5%. 82.5% > 82%, so Kai has the higher score.

items.q: Four shops have a sale on the same trainers. Which sign gives the biggest discount?
items.e: As percentages: 13 = 33.3…%, 30%, 14 = 25%. 35% is the biggest, so 35% off.

items.q: There are 50 pupils in Year 6. 23 of them cycle to school. What percentage cycle?
items.e: 2350 = 46100 (multiply the top and bottom by 2) = 46%. 27% uses the 27 pupils who do not cycle.

items.q: Lily’s sunflower is 0.375 m tall. What fraction of a metre is that?
items.e: 0.375 = 3751000. Divide the top and bottom by 125: 38 m. 375100 m would be 3.75 m.

items.q: £2 is shared equally between 5 children. How much does each child get?
items.e: £2 ÷ 5 = 25 of £1 = 410 = £0.40 = 40p. £2.50 is 5 ÷ 2, the wrong way round.

items.q: At PE, Arjun hits the target 7 times out of 8. Zara hits it 85% of the time. Who is more accurate?
items.e: 78 = 7 ÷ 8 = 0.875 = 87.5%. 87.5% > 85%, so Arjun is more accurate.

items.q: A bag holds 1 kg of flour. Leo uses 0.4 kg to make bread. What percentage of the bag does he use?
items.e: 0.4 kg out of 1 kg is 0.4 of the bag. 0.4 = 40100 = 40%. 60% is what is left.

items.q: A quiz has 20 questions. Alfie gets 0.85 of them right. How many questions does he get right?
items.e: 0.85 = 85100 = 1720. 1720 of 20 questions is 17 questions. 3 is the number he gets wrong, and 8.5 is 0.85 × 10.

items.q: A water bottle holds 1 litre. Jack drinks 0.35 litres. What fraction of the bottle is left?
items.e: 1 − 0.35 = 0.65 litres are left. 0.65 = 65100 = 1320 (divide by 5). 720 is the part he drank.
